description_full: COSCO SHIPPING Development Co., Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, research, develops, manufactures, and sells containers in the United States, Asia, Hong Kong, Mainland China, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Container Manufacturing Business; Shipping Leasing Business; Container Leasing Business; and Investment Management Business segments. The company offers dry cargo, refrigerated, and special containers, as well as container houses and after-sales services; integrated shipping, logistics, and industry finance services; and vessel chartering and financial leasing services, including container ships, dry bulk carriers, special-purpose vessels, and tankers. COSCO SHIPPING Development Co., Ltd. was formerly known as China Shipping Container Lines Company Limited and changed its name to COSCO SHIPPING Development Co., Ltd. in November 2016. COSCO SHIPPING Development Co., Ltd. was founded in 1997 and is headquartered in Shanghai, China.

financial_summary: Cosco Shipping Development Co L is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.4B market cap on $3.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 24% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $667M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 12.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 46.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 3.0% of the shares.
